### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e33f6012a0e5b3af903f77d95448700253c41fd1` — the merge of head `be88f869448ce366f0e085c4fb52f7535bb02083` into base `ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e33f6012a0e5b3af903f77d95448700253c41fd1 && git checkout e33f6012a0e5b3af903f77d95448700253c41fd1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 be88f869448ce366f0e085c4fb52f7535bb02083 && git checkout -B drift-repro ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182 && git merge --no-ff be88f869448ce366f0e085c4fb52f7535bb02083

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec6b5fd3464ce5413691a7cab810d1c19db50182
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**CI failure at head 0f8d050e is not this PR's: the checkout step timed out.**

- `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (job 133695937589, run 43980637506) failed in its "Checkout repository" step. `git fetch` hung, and the runner logged "The action 'Checkout repository' has timed out after 25 minutes".
- No gate step ran in that job. Every step after checkout was skipped. The closing `lane-verdict.mjs` then failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, because there was no checked-out tree. That error follows from the empty checkout and is not a gate result.
- `Lint & Repo Gates` (job 133707770255) is the aggregator. Its only problem line is `lint lane lint-ci-engine concluded failure -- expected success`. The other seven lint lanes report `ok`.
- None of this PR's diff ran in the failed job: the two objectql cascade files, the objectql test, the service-automation integration test and the changeset.
- At the same head, every sibling lane that actually ran is green: Type Check (workspace, consumer, source, debt ledger), ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates and all three scoped lanes. Test Core 2/8 through 8/8 are green too.
- Head 0f8d050e is unchanged. No new commit. A dev does not re-run jobs (`scripts/pm/rerun-failed.mjs`), so re-running job 133695937589 is left to the seat.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · REWORK (1 item)** · head `8ba1ea555ec26fe6b61e56f0112e352131ed3d5d` · card #33699 · read 2026-11-17T00:06Z

Code read in parallel with CI, as the seat asked. This head's CI was still running at the reading (3 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 16 `in_progress`), so this verdict could not have been an ACCEPT here in any case; the item below moves the head anyway.

### REWORK

1. **The forget before a `set_null` clear is not pinned.** `walkReferencingRelations` drops the kept probes at two writes: before a relation's cascaded children are deleted (`engine-cascade-planning.ts`, the `cascaded.length > 0` branch) and before each `set_null` clear (the `forgetCollectedProbes(cascadeSet)` just above the `multiValued` branch). Ablation 2 in the body removes only the first; the two new `[c1]` cases and the recycle-bin pin all go through a cascaded child's delete. Remove the forget before the clear and nothing goes red, yet it is the only guard for this order: a `set_null` relation walked before a cascading one, whose clear runs an update hook that writes a row of the later cascading relation. The walk then takes the collection's answer, misses that row, and the row survives the delete pointing at a removed parent. Add one case in the `[c1]` describe for that order (a hook on the `set_null` child's update writes a dependent the next cascading probe must find and delete), and record in the body the ablation of that forget turning it red.

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #33699`. Closing-keyword scan of the whole body: one hit, `#33699`. `Fixes` agrees with the area's choice (A) and with the card's remaining item being c1 of ruling 6893104201.
- **File surface:** 5 files from `get_files`: two `packages/objectql/src` sources, their test, the changeset, and the one forced test change in `packages/services/service-automation`, which claim amendment 6933000296 covers. Nothing else.
- **Merge commit:** `8ba1ea55` merges `main` into `0f8d050e`; `git diff origin/main...8ba1ea55` shows only the 5 files above.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/33699-cascade-probe-read-once.md`, `@objectstack/objectql` patch; `@objectstack/service-automation` is touched by a test only. Sentences checked against the diff: "takes the collection's answer for each probe it repeats, until its own first write" (`takeCollectedProbe` / `forgetCollectedProbes`); "every probe after that first write reads as before" (the map is deleted, so every later take answers `undefined`); "The recycle-bin snapshot keeps its own read" (`RecycleBinCapture.onCollected` still calls `driver.find`). The 58 → 57 figure is a statement count, not a timing, and the read-order pin (12 driver reads to 11) shows the same one-read difference deterministically; accepted as written.
- **Behaviour-neutral premise, read in the source:** between `collectCascadeDeleteSet` and `walkReferencingRelations` only `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade` and `onCollected` run (`cascadeDeleteRelations`), and `onCollected` only reads (`capture.ts:220`, `driver.find`). Collection and walk get the same `fresh` array. The key is the exact ids in order and type, so any mismatch (a duplicate id the collection filtered, a reordered frontier) misses and reads; it cannot reuse a wrong answer. A joining member's walk has no kept map and reads.
- **Forced test change:** `delete-record-predicate-walk-batched.integration.test.ts` moves `detail: 6` to `detail: 3`; that pin counted exactly the repeated read this item removes, and the comment names the ruling. `link` and `tags` stay at 3.
- **Tests and controls:** two new `[c1]` cases (exact read order; a child's `beforeDelete` writing a late row of the next relation, which is still deleted). Ablations 1 and 2 recorded with what went red. Suites: objectql 605 files / 13511 tests at the code commit, the later commits touching nothing under `packages/objectql`.
- **L2:** not owed. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `(narrowing)`, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path. Agreed with the area's reading.
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34507`: 0 of 5 paths governed, 173 changed lines (+166 / −7) ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing by the area after L1 ACCEPT on a green head.

### Out of scope, for the area to place

- **Acceptance notes, "Observation, not filed":** the predicate arm's read-door question for the batch runs twice, and without the transaction tag the other cascade statements carry. A read outside the cascade's transaction may be a defect of its own; it needs a disposition line before ACCEPT (`filed #N`, or `dropped — reason`), not silence.
- **Body, not the head:** the first line of the body is the area's signature; the attribution comment and the "Requested by" line are meant to be its first two lines. A body edit, no push.

### Next

L1 reads the delta only, on a head whose CI is green and announced final in a PR comment.

### Delta read (`git diff 8ba1ea555 be88f869`: 1 commit, 1 test file, +28 / −2)

- **REWORK item 1, closed.** `be88f869` adds `a row a set_null clear's hook writes is still found by the next cascading relation's probe` to the `[c1]` describe. `makeEngine({ parentLookup: true })` gives `acct` a self `set_null` lookup, so the walk clears `a2.parent` before it reaches `line`, whose probe the collection already read; an `afterUpdate` hook on that clear writes `l9` under `a1`. The case asserts `a2.parent` is `null`, no `line` row survives, and the write order `deleteMany line l1,l2,l3`, `delete line l9`, `delete acct a1`. No source line moves.

- **Body, no head move:** the observation now reads `dropped` with its reason (one predicate asked twice in one transaction, no wrong answer) and #34533 is closed `not_planned`. It also corrects the earlier note: the statements do carry the transaction tag. The attribution comment and the "Requested by" line now open the body.
